sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Collections are the backbone of every Java application. Interviewers use them to probe memory understanding (how HashMap works), algorithmic thinking (choosing the right structure), and thread-safety awareness. A fresher who can explain HashMap's bucket-chain structure is instantly memorable.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **List** = ordered, allows duplicates. **ArrayList** = array-backed (O(1) get). **LinkedList** = doubly-linked (O(1) add/remove at ends).
- **Map** = key→value pairs. **HashMap** = hashing (O(1) avg). **TreeMap** = sorted keys (O(log n)). **LinkedHashMap** = insertion order.
- **Set** = unique elements. **HashSet** uses HashMap internally; **TreeSet** = sorted.
- **Queue** = FIFO. **PriorityQueue** = heap-based ordering. **Deque** = double-ended.
- **HashMap internals**: index = hash(key) % capacity → bucket (linked list or tree in Java 8+ when > 8 entries).
- **fail-fast iterators** throw ConcurrentModificationException if collection is structurally modified during iteration.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **list-basics**: ArrayList resizes at 1.5x; LinkedList has O(n) get by index — never use it for random access.
- **map-basics**: equals() and hashCode() contract is critical for HashMap keys; break it and put/get will fail.
- **set-basics**: HashSet.add() returns false if element already exists; this is how duplicates are detected.
- **queue-deque-basics**: PriorityQueue is a min-heap by default; use Collections.reverseOrder() for max-heap.
- **collections-utility-methods**: Collections.unmodifiableList wraps a list (original is still mutable!); List.of is truly immutable.
- **iterator-and-foreach**: Use Iterator.remove() to safely remove during iteration; enhanced for-each hides the iterator.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"How does HashMap work internally?"* — Hash the key, compute bucket index, store in array of linked lists (or red-black tree for buckets > 8).
- *"What is ConcurrentModificationException?"* — Thrown by fail-fast iterators when the collection is structurally modified outside the iterator.
- *"What happens if two keys have the same hashCode?"* — Hash collision → they go into the same bucket as a linked list; equals() then distinguishes them.
- *"What is the difference between List.of() and Collections.unmodifiableList()?"* — List.of() is immutable; unmodifiableList is a read-only view of a mutable list.
- *"Why must you override hashCode when you override equals?"* — Objects that are equals() must return the same hashCode; violating this breaks HashMap lookup.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"HashMap works by hashing the key to get a bucket index, then storing the entry in that bucket — and when two keys hash to the same bucket, they form a linked list, so equals() is used to find the right entry during get."*
